findings.title: Watering requests have no timeout: a hung POST leaves 'Saving…' / 'Watering…' spinning forever
findings.steps: On /beds open 'Record past watering' for North bed, enter 7.5 L, make POST /api/waterings hang (browser_route never responding), click Save watering, wait 12 s.
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 s with a visible error, and the button becomes usable again.
findings.actual: The button still says 'Saving…' and stays disabled after 12 s with no message. 'Water now' behaves the same. The API client ($fetch.create in useApi.ts) sets no timeout.
findings.evidence: After 12 s the bed card text showed 'Saving…' and no error.

findings.title: Watering on a second bed re-enables the first bed's in-flight save, so it can be submitted twice
findings.steps: While North bed's 'Save watering' (or 'Water now') request is pending, click 'Water now' on Shade corner.
findings.expected: North bed's button stays disabled until its own request finishes.
findings.actual: wateringBedId is a single shared ref, so it switches to Shade corner. North bed's 'Save watering' and 'Water now' are enabled again while the first request is still pending, and a second click records a duplicate watering. When either request finishes, wateringBedId is reset to null, so the other bed's button is enabled again too. waterError/waterNotice are shared the same way, so one bed's error or notice replaces the other's.
findings.evidence: After clicking Water now on Shade corner, North bed's button read 'Save watering' and was enabled while its POST was still hanging.

findings.title: Retrying a watering after a lost response records it twice (no idempotency)
findings.steps: Click Water now (or Save watering). The server commits but the response is lost or times out. Click again.
findings.actual: The request carries no idempotency key or client request id, so each retry inserts a new row.
findings.evidence: Code reading: create_watering always inserts; recordWatering sends no key.

findings.title: Error states for recent waterings (dashboard) and the waterings list have no Retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/waterings return 500, then go to the dashboard or Waterings through an in-app link. Restore the server.
findings.expected: The error message comes with a Retry button that reloads the data in place.
findings.actual: The pages show only 'Could not load recent waterings.' / 'Could not load waterings.' with no way to retry short of reloading the page or changing the filter. On the dashboard, refresh is not even taken from wateringsResult.
findings.evidence: dashClient: 'Recent waterings / All waterings / Could not load recent waterings.' with no button. /waterings: 'Could not load waterings.' with no button.

findings.title: Waterings filter silently loses its bed options when /api/beds fails
findings.expected: A visible error says the bed list could not load.
findings.actual: The beds error is never read (only data is destructured). The select shows only 'All beds', and with ?bed=1 the filter shows no selected bed even though the list is filtered.
findings.evidence: Code: `const { data: beds } = bedsResult`, with no error handling.

findings.title: Waterings tables overflow 375 px width with long bed names
findings.steps: Create a bed named '🌻Ünïcødéx' followed by 40 W's, water it, then view the dashboard and /waterings at 375 px wide.
findings.expected: The page fits 375 px and long names wrap.
findings.actual: The page scrolls sideways. The Bed and Amount columns extend to x=809–929 px.
findings.evidence: scrollWidth was 886 on / and 971 on /waterings at a 375 px viewport.

findings.title: Past-watering form squashes Date and Litres inputs to ~30 px at 375 px
findings.steps: At 375 px wide, open 'Record past watering' on a bed.
findings.expected: The Date and Litres inputs are wide enough to use and read.
findings.actual: The grid '1fr 1fr auto' gives the buttons their full width, leaving each input about 30–40 px wide, so the chosen date and amount cannot be read.
findings.evidence: Element screenshot: the Date and Litres boxes are tiny. Input right edges were at 75 and 116 px, while the buttons ended at 329 px.

findings.title: Bed ids or watering ids beyond 64-bit cause 500 errors
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error, because SQLite raises an OverflowError on the integer.
findings.evidence: curl returned 'Internal Server Error 500' for all three requests.

findings.title: Tiny litre amounts are accepted but shown as '0 L'
findings.steps: Record a past watering with litres 0.001 (the form has novalidate and accepts it, and the API allows any value > 0).
findings.expected: The value is either refused with a reason (the input says min 0.1) or shown accurately.
findings.actual: It is stored and then displayed as '0 L' on the dashboard and on the waterings list, and in the success message.
findings.evidence: The API returned 201 with litres 0.001, and the dashboard row showed '1 Nov 2026  North bed  0 L'.

findings.title: API accepts a boolean as litres
'Today' differs between browser and server, so today's watering can be refused as 'in the future'
findings.steps: Use a browser whose time zone is ahead of the server's (e.g. the browser is past midnight while the server is not). Record a past watering for the default date, today.
findings.expected: The date the form offers by default (todayIso, browser local) is accepted.
findings.actual: The server checks against date.today() in its own time zone and returns 'Watering date cannot be in the future.' 'Water now' also stores watered_on as the server-local date, which can differ from the user's day.
findings.evidence: Code: not_in_future uses date.today(), while the client's max and default use the browser's local date.
